summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Seddon Park commenced with high tactical intensity as New Zealand posted 519/7 (144.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, West Indies countered with 138/9 (63.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Kane Williamson 251 (412b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Kane Williamson delivered a masterclass for New Zealand (251 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (New Zealand 57%) and allowing New Zealand to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, West Indies faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. New Zealand's bowling unit, bolstered by KA Jamieson (51 Runs & 4 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing New Zealand won by innings & 134 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: New Zealand's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While West Indies produced fighting phases, New Zealand won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
